title: Hospital station cannot add or induct totes
user_facing_summary: Troubleshoot a hospital-station flow where totes cannot be added or inducted, especially when tote removal still works or an AGV appears in an unexpected location.
playbook_goal: Determine whether the hospital induction failure is associated with an abnormal AGV location, roster state, or tote association, then guide authorized recovery and validate that hospital tote add and remove operations work again.
observed_entry_symptoms: The hospital station cannot add or induct totes.
Totes can be removed but cannot be added at the hospital.
A robot or AGV is reported in a shut down state.
An AGV appears not to belong in the displayed location, or two AGVs appear under the same rack or in the same zone.
Hospital backlog or tote flow disruption is reported.
negative_or_absent_signals: The packet does not establish that the entire site is down for every occurrence of this symptom.
The packet does not confirm a single root cause; the removed-AGV and associated-tote explanation is explicitly presented as a possibility.
The packet does not provide a confirmed live alarm code or exact service state for the hospital station.
support_user_language_examples: Totes can come out but not go in
Hospital tote add is not working
AGV is in the wrong spot
Two AGVs are under the rack
tentative_internal_patterns: Possible AGV-to-tote association left behind after AGV removal
Possible AGV roster, location, or rack-position mismatch
Possible hospital-station service or server abnormality
internal_pattern_notes: These are tentative patterns from chat, work-order notes, and screenshots. The packet does not confirm that any one pattern caused the failure.
separability_reason: This flow can be selected directly from the distinct observable symptom that hospital tote addition or induction fails, including the reported remove-versus-add asymmetry. Its troubleshooting goal is to restore hospital tote-flow state, independent of the separate site-wide sort availability flow.
confidence_reason: The packet repeatedly documents hospital inability to add or induct totes, AGV location and tote-association anomalies, high-level corrective actions, and successful validation that totes could again be added and removed.

title: Site cannot start or sustain sort
user_facing_summary: Troubleshoot a broad operational outage where the site cannot start sort or stops during sort, with possible server or service abnormality and subsequent recovery validation.
playbook_goal: Determine whether the report represents a site-wide sort availability problem, assess the source-supported service or server recovery direction, and validate stable operation without treating the historical service hypothesis as confirmed cause.
observed_entry_symptoms: The site goes down in the middle of sort.
Movement stops or the system is not running.
A work-order or repair note reports AGV hospital-station server issues and a need to reset services.

The packet does not establish that the server or service condition was the sole cause of the site-wide disruption.
The hospital-specific tote and AGV anomalies may coexist with, precede, or contribute to the broader outage; their relationship is not confirmed.

tentative_internal_patterns: Possible OptiSweep or AGV-server service abnormality

internal_pattern_notes: The source reports service reset and Hospital Lane restart in closure details, while other messages describe AGV and tote corrections. These are source-supported recovery observations, not confirmed causal classifications.
separability_reason: This flow has a different entry pattern—site-wide inability to start or sustain sort—and a different troubleshooting goal—restore overall operational availability. It is independently reusable from the hospital-only tote-induction flow, although it may branch to that flow when hospital symptoms are also present.
confidence_reason: The packet clearly documents site-down and sort-start failure reports, server/service-reset notes, a high-level OptiSweep service reset and Hospital Lane restart, and later reports that movement and the system resumed. Exact service diagnosis and validation evidence are incomplete.

nodes.title: Stop if service recovery or sort validation fails
nodes.intent: Hand off when the service or server condition cannot be confirmed, authorized recovery does not restore operation, or the site remains unable to start or sustain sort.
nodes.goal: Hand off when the service or server condition cannot be confirmed, authorized recovery does not restore operation, or the site remains unable to start or sustain sort.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed to prepare escalation evidence including service or server observations, Event Viewer or Windows Services evidence when available, sort availability reports, Hospital Lane state, recovery actions attempted, and validation results, with stop criteria and the receiving technical role.
nodes.source_supported_description: The source contains incomplete service evidence, an unreadable dashboard artifact, and a site-wide outage that eventually recovered through multiple actions.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed to prepare escalation evidence including service or server observations, Event Viewer or Windows Services evidence when available, sort availability reports, Hospital Lane state, recovery actions attempted, and validation results, with stop criteria and the receiving technical role.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: L1/L2 support observes unresolved service abnormality, failed recovery, repeated outage, or insufficient evidence to continue safely. Healthy signal for this gate is a complete evidence package and controlled handoff, not continued troubleshooting. Unhealthy continuation signal: repeated resets, unsupported changes, or declaring recovery from a single unverified status message.

source_used_surfaces.source_evidence: The packet includes an artifact categorized as Windows-services-related, but notes that the visible crop is not a live service console.
Site-down, sort-start failure, movement recovery, and system-running reports are present in Teams.

unhealthy_indicators: Sort remains unavailable after the supported recovery path.
The site repeatedly goes down or cannot start sort.
Further recovery would require unsupported or unauthorized changes.
inconclusive_indicators: Only an unreadable dashboard or historical notes entry is available.
The service name or current state cannot be identified.
nodes.stop_or_escalation_note: Historical unfamiliarity, support participation, and communication delays are not themselves escalation conditions; escalation is based on unsafe, unsupported, or unresolved technical state.
